lessons.title: Practice Window Functions
lessons.description: For each department, rank employees by salary descending with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC). Name that column rank. The test checks that you return at least 5 rows and a column named rank.
lessons.starter_code:
-- TODO: add rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)
SELECT first_name, department, salary FROM employees WHERE 0;
lessons.solution_code: SELECT first_name, department, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees;

source.name: SQLite official documentation (sqlite.org) — Window functions — 'input values are taken from a window of one or more rows'

learning_objectives: Attic clerks recount crates before dawn, and compute per-row results without collapsing rows using OVER.

exercises.question: Attic clerks recount crates before dawn. For compute per-row results without collapsing rows using OVER, which line ranks employees by salary?
hints: Compare each line with the example.
One line matches the example.
RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC)
exercises.explanation: RANK over salary descending puts the highest salary at place 1.

exercises.question: Attic clerks recount crates before dawn. For compute per-row results without collapsing rows using OVER, what value is displayed?
hints: Run the example in your head from the top.
The last line is what gets displayed.
exercises.explanation: The Window Functions program displays that value.
exercises.starter_code: SELECT name FROM (SELECT first_name AS name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS place FROM employees) ranked WHERE place = 1;
